title: Police officer cleared in fatal shooting: Stittsville man shot after stabbing wife
article: An Ottawa-Carleton police officer has been cleared in the Oct. 4 fatal shooting of a Stittsville man, who repeatedly stabbed his wife and two elderly neighbours before being shot dead by the officer.
The province's Special Investigations Unit announced its decision yesterday after investigating the officer's actions and her role in the death of Frank Hutterer, 35.
Six SIU investigators investigated the shooting, which centred around a violent domestic dispute that spilled into the quiet street in front of the couple's Stittsville bungalow.
The incident began at about 9 a.m. with repeated calls to 911 for police assistance involving a domestic dispute at a house belonging to Mr. Hutterer and his wife, Sally McIntyre.

When police arrived, they found Ms. McIntyre lying on the side of Cordukes Street, bleeding from several knife wounds, and two elderly neighbours, Mitch Smith, 71 and his wife, Margaret, 69, from across the street, both suffering from defence wounds after trying to intervene in the dispute.
When the first officer arrived on scene, she was faced with an enraged suspect, who witnesses said wielded knives in both hands as he moved towards the officer.
The officer's repeated commands to stop went unheeded and the officer fired what witnesses said was four shots before Mr. Hutterer fell dead to the ground.
SIU director Peter Tinsley said his investigators concluded that it was reasonable for the officer to have believed that her life and the lives of others were in immediate danger.
The elderly couple were treated at hospital and released the same day of the shooting.
Ms. McIntyre continues to recover from her wounds and was able to attend last week's funeral for her husband in Alliston, north of Toronto. She could not be reached for comment.
The SIU investigates all cases where police action results in death or serious injury to a civilian.
